verdict.rationale: Clerk's docs describe Organizations as a first-party feature for building multi-tenant B2B apps. Users can belong to multiple organizations, and each session carries organization context (memberships, roles, active organization). Default admin/member roles plus custom roles are documented, and drop-in UI components cover creating and switching organizations and viewing memberships and invitations. Missing for 10: detailed documentation of the invitation flow itself (sending, accepting, revoking invites), and independent hands-on corroboration of the organization features.

support.subject: As a developer, I can model multi-tenant B2B apps with organizations, memberships, and invitation flows out of the box

citations.quote: Organizations let you group users with Roles and Permissions. This lets you build multi-tenant B2B apps like Slack (workspaces), Linear (teams), or Vercel (projects) where users switch between different team contexts.
Users can belong to multiple Organizations, and Clerk provides the Organization context (memberships, Roles, and the Active Organization) in each session.
Allow your users to create new organizations, switch between accounts, manage settings and billing, and view memberships and invitations.
Drop-in UI components for authentication, profile management, organization management, and billing.
